transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-08-03
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~42 minutes
Attendees: Alex Chen (Redwood AE), Priya Nair (Redwood SE), Liam O'Connor (Redwood CSM), Jordan Lee (CTO - Aperture), Marta Reyes (Eng Lead), Samir Patel (SRE), Evelyn Wu (Product)
Shared: QBR deck (link), cost_spreadsheet.csv (link), incident timelines doc (link)

[00:00:05] Alex Chen: hey everyone, thanks for taking the time for the qbr, um we wanted to run through usage, costs, reliability and then roadmap alignment. i think Priya and Liam are on as well to cover the technical and cs bits.

[00:00:20] Jordan Lee: yeah thanks alex, um sounds good. we've got a couple of folks on the call who care about perf and billing so we'll be concise.

[00:00:34] Liam O'Connor: quick agenda, maybe 10 mins on usage/costs, 10 on incidents and reliability, 10 on roadmap and model changes, then next steps. cool?

[00:00:45] Marta Reyes: works for us.

[00:01:05] Alex Chen: okay, first slide — usage trends. aperture's total token volume is up ~20% month over month, driven by the new RAG flow in support chat. top routes are support-chat, summarization-batch, and doc-embedding jobs. biggest growth is support-chat, long contexts.

[00:01:40] Evelyn Wu: yea that's right, the new summarize+context approach increased the average prompt size — we now send ~4k tokens per request on support-chat when the thread is long.

[00:01:58] Priya Nair: that aligns with what we see — long-sequence generation pushes you into higher kernel costs and also reduces batching efficiency. there were a couple of spikes last month where batching dropped because requests were pinned to a single worker due to session affinity.

[00:02:22] Samir Patel: quick q — i flagged a cost spike two weeks ago, looked like a multiplier on the token costs for a few days, do you have visibility on what happened?

[00:02:34] Alex Chen: yeah we pulled the billing, and that period correlates with a model change on your side — you switched from our default 8k context to the longer-context variant, and combined with an increase in concurrent threads it amplified. Priya, do you want to add?

[00:02:49] Priya Nair: sure. so the long-context variant is more expensive per token and we saw fewer opportunities to batch because the request sizes were variable. also there was an instance of a retry storm when a worker briefly returned 503s which prevented batching for ~30 mins on the morning of July 14th. that looks like the incident Samir referenced.

[00:03:15] Samir Patel: yes july 14th, that was the one. we saw p95 latency jump and our autoscaler spun up more containers which increased cost.

[00:03:28] Marta Reyes: any tuning we can do on the batching side? our engineering team is open to changes but we need low latency.

[00:03:35] Priya Nair: a few levers. one, prefix/KV caching for recurring conversational contexts — that reduces re-encoding long history. two, segmented batching: prioritize low-latency single-turn requests separate from long RAG generations. three, quantization profiles on the model variants — you could run 4-bit or 8-bit in non-critical routes to save tokens/compute. each has tradeoffs.

[00:04:05] Jordan Lee: when you say KV caching, is that something on our side or handled by Redwood?

[00:04:11] Priya Nair: Redwood runtime supports prefix/KV cache. we can enable it per-route — it's transparent to your app, you just need to opt-in and provide cache keys. we'll send a runbook.

[00:04:25] Alex Chen: also from a cost viewpoint, we noticed a couple of long-running batch jobs that were scheduled during business hours, you could shift heavy embedding runs to off-peak to get better batching and lower cost.

[00:04:38] Evelyn Wu: good call, we can reschedule.

[00:04:45] Priya Nair: on the reliability incidents — we pulled the three incidents in the last quarter: July 14th worker retry storm, May 2nd increased tail latency due to a model warmup issue, and March 27th networking flake in the region. we've documented mitigations: better autoscaler thresholds, pre-warm for large-model deployments, and fallback routing to the secondary region.

[00:05:15] Samir Patel: the pre-warm sounds helpful because we do see cold-starts when traffic shifts. how long is warmup for the larger context variant?

[00:05:23] Priya Nair: typically 30-90 seconds depending on the model and GPU type. with pre-warm policies you can keep a minimal pool hot and spin up to handle bursts. that's what Dedicated helps with too.

[00:05:38] Jordan Lee: let's talk about Dedicated/VPC — we've been evaluating it because of compliance and predictability. what are the main differences vs hosted?

[00:05:47] Alex Chen: short answer: Dedicated is reserved capacity in your cloud region with pinned GPUs, predictable throughput and lower variance in latency; Hosted is multi-tenant with better elasticity but more variability. VPC option gives private networking and customer-managed keys. pricing model shifts from per-token to committed monthly capacity with overage.

[00:06:09] Marta Reyes: curious about onboarding complexity — we have internal compliance reqs (SOC2, SSO/SAML, audit logs). how does that map?

[00:06:18] Liam O'Connor: we support SSO/SAML, SOC2 artifacts for Dedicated and Private, and audit logs with retention options. for VPC on cloud we do a private control plane option; for fully on-prem we have a packaged deployment but that's heavier. we can share the security pack.

[00:06:34] Evelyn Wu: cost-wise, when does Dedicated become cheaper? our token volume varies but is trending up.

[00:06:41] Alex Chen: it depends on committed throughput and utilization. if you need consistent low-latency and have predictable spikes, Dedicated can lower your per-token compute cost but you trade off commitment. we'll model scenarios in the cost sheet — that's one of the next steps.

[00:06:58] Jordan Lee: and data residency? we need EU logs to remain in EU for some customers.

[00:07:04] Priya Nair: yes we can pin region for Dedicated and keep logs in-region; for Hosted we can route EU traffic to zone-specific clusters. we'll include region mapping in the proposal.

[00:07:18] Marta Reyes: Model roadmap — you mentioned a vetted performance profile for upcoming model upgrade, what are compatibility notes for our RAG flow?

[00:07:28] Priya Nair: the new 2026.3 model has improved long-context attention and better tokenization for code and technical language, so RAG quality should improve. however resource usage per token is slightly higher, so we recommend a canary period and A/B tests. Redwood Optimize can suggest quantization and batching config adjustments automatically.

[00:07:50] Alex Chen: also note that we offer automatic fallbacks: if the long-context variant is unavailable, requests can route to a compatible shorter-context variant to avoid failures. that'll affect quality but keeps availability.

[00:08:05] Samir Patel: for the July 14th 503s, is fallback routing something we could've used?

[00:08:10] Priya Nair: yes, we saw the retries came from affinity to a single zone; a fallback policy would've routed some traffic to other regions or model variants. we can help set up the policy.

[00:08:24] Jordan Lee: security question — encryption at rest keys: can we bring our own key (BYOK) for Dedicated?

[00:08:30] Liam O'Connor: yes, KMS integration is supported for Dedicated and Private; for Hosted we offer managed keys and an option for customer-managed KMS in certain enterprise tiers. we'll confirm in the security packet.

[00:08:44] Marta Reyes: okay practical ask — we'd like a plan to cap monthly spend while we test Dedicated. any recommendations?

[00:08:52] Alex Chen: two paths: 1) run a short pilot Dedicated with a modest commit and strict guardrails (alerts, quotas), 2) stick to Hosted and implement auto-scaling and batch tuning plus spend alerts. for the pilot we can recommend the GPU flavor and commit that best matches your p95 latency target.

[00:09:12] Evelyn Wu: what about a hybrid routing? critical routes on Dedicated, bulk embeddings on Hosted?

[00:09:18] Priya Nair: absolutely supported — Smart routing can direct by route or SLA tier. many customers use Dedicated for low-latency interactive routes and Hosted for bulk workloads.

[00:09:30] Jordan Lee: great. can you also include a breakdown of our per-route spend? the spreadsheet shows aggregate but we need per-endpoint.

[00:09:39] Alex Chen: yes we'll include per-route token counts and cost allocation. that's part of the next steps.

[00:09:50] Marta Reyes: on monitoring — we saw a gap where one of our alerts didn't trigger because the trace tags were missing. any suggestions?

[00:09:58] Priya Nair: ensure trace tags are included in the request metadata and use per-route tracing hooks. Redwood Console supports token-level and route-level dashboards; we can help map your Prometheus alerts to console metrics.

[00:10:15] Samir Patel: for the technical deep dive, can we cover KV cache keys and session affinity? that's likely the root cause for the batching drop.

[00:10:22] Priya Nair: yes we'll add it to the deep dive agenda. we'll run an ops checklist: cache key strategy, session affinity settings, autoscaler thresholds, and fallback policies.

[00:10:35] Alex Chen: quick recap of recommended action: enable prefix/KV caching for support-chat, reschedule heavy embed jobs to off-peak, run a small Dedicated pilot proposal, and Priya will lead the technical deep dive.

[00:10:50] Jordan Lee: sounds good. any open risk items?

[00:10:54] Priya Nair: risk: if you move to the new model without canarying, you might see temporary quality regressions or cost change. mitigation: A/B test and rollback rules. Also, the trial Dedicated commit needs to be sized correctly to avoid underutilization.

[00:11:12] Evelyn Wu: on the A/B testing — does Redwood support traffic split and canary analytics?

[00:11:17] Liam O'Connor: yes, we support canary percentages, per-route model pins, and sample-based quality metrics if you provide evaluation prompts. we can integrate with your eval harness.

[00:11:30] Alex Chen: time check — maybe two quick questions from aperture before we wrap?

[00:11:35] Marta Reyes: one — latency SLOs: what are realistic p95 numbers for the long-context variant on our region?

[00:11:42] Priya Nair: on the GPU type you currently use (A100-equivalent), p95 for long-context generation is around 450-700ms depending on sequence length; p99 can be higher. for Dedicated we usually see narrower p95 variance. we'll put concrete numbers in the deck.

[00:12:00] Jordan Lee: second — compliance artifacts, can you share SOC2 Type II and your network diagrams?

[00:12:07] Liam O'Connor: yes we'll attach SOC2 report and the network architecture diagrams in the follow-up.

[00:12:15] Samir Patel: quick operational ask — can we get a monthly digest of incidents and a short RCA for each?

[00:12:21] Liam O'Connor: yes we can provide a monthly incident digest and attach RCAs for Sev2+ events.

[00:12:30] Alex Chen: great. last part — roadmap alignment. do you have any product roadmap items we should be aware of that might change load patterns?

[00:12:38] Evelyn Wu: we're planning an in-app knowledge base rollout and a new summarization batch job in Q4 which could increase embedding volume by 3x.

[00:12:47] Priya Nair: good to know — embedding increases are predictable load; batching and scheduling will help. for knowledge-base interactive read flows, consider Dedicated for the low-latency parts.

[00:12:58] Jordan Lee: okay let's wrap. can we capture the explicit next steps?

[00:13:02] Alex Chen: yes — (1) Alex to send detailed cost breakdown and per-route usage by 2026-08-07; (2) Priya & Samir technical deep dive proposed 2026-08-11; (3) Liam to attach QBR deck and benchmarks to CRM by 2026-08-05; (4) Aperture to share 2-week sample traces by 2026-08-10.

[00:13:23] Marta Reyes: thanks, appreciate the clear items.

[00:13:28] Alex Chen: thanks all. we'll follow up in email and log the action items. talk soon.

[00:13:35] Jordan Lee: thanks everyone. bye.

[00:13:45] (call ends)

Notes on quality: transcription had some mis-heard product names (red wood dedicated -> redwood dedicated) and timestamps are approximate.
